notes: Official sources could not be opened: textbooksonline.tn.nic.in and e-learn.tnschools.gov.in refuse automated fetching via robots.txt, tnschools.gov.in and scert.tnschools.gov.in are JavaScript apps that returned no content, and the sandbox shell has no internet access. Because of this every chapter is marked verified:false. Chapter titles were cross-checked between two independent secondary sites (Shaalaa and Brainkart), which agree on every chapter title and order. Neither is official.

Edition currency for 2026-27: DT Next (8 May 2026; 16 Aug 2026) reports that only Classes 1-3 received new-syllabus books in 2026-27. Classes 4-12 continue on the existing Samacheer Kalvi syllabus (the 2018-19 / 2019-20 'new syllabus' books), and the new State Education Policy curriculum is targeted for 2027-28. The same article says Classes 4-12 books with the old syllabus were 'being prepared' for 2026-27, so a 2026 reprint or re-typeset printing may exist. I could not see its imprint page to confirm the edition line or any content changes.

Section titles come from Brainkart's topic index for this book, which follows the textbook's headings. They were not checked against the official PDF. I dropped exercise, summary, 'Try these' and worked-example entries and kept only content headings. Section ids are positional, not the textbook's own section numbers, which I could not see.
All outcomes are my own paraphrases of chapter content; no textbook text is reproduced.
Competencies listed under 'proposed' are reused across the TN Grade 6, 7 and 8 files with identical ids and definitions.

TERM STRUCTURE DIFFERS FROM THE BRIEF. The brief said Grades 6-8 are term-wise, but DT Next (Aug 2026) reports that Class 8 moved to a single annual textbook about three years ago, and that only Classes 6-7 (and 1-5) still have three term books. Shaalaa, Brainkart and StudiesToday all show one Class 8 Mathematics book with chapters 1-7 numbered straight through. I therefore set textbook.terms = null and term = null, and used ids of the form tn-g08-c01, the schema's pattern for a non-term book. If OpenPath needs a term split for Grade 8, check the official PDF (textbooksonline.tn.nic.in) or the school calendar before imposing one. I did not invent one.
Chapter titles, order and exercise counts (1.1-1.7, 2.1-2.4, 3.1-3.10, 4.1-4.5, 5.1-5.5, 6.1-6.3, 7.1-7.4) agree between Shaalaa and Brainkart.

Chapter 2 'Parts of a Circle' covers arcs and sectors, which I mapped as an exact fit to MATH.measurement.sectors even though the list places that competency at Grade 10. Chapter 2 '3-D shapes' (nets and Euler's formula) is my reading of the section title; the exact sub-content was not seen.

Chapter 6 Statistics: the sections cover graphical representation of ungrouped and grouped frequency distributions. I assume that means bar graphs, histograms and frequency polygons, and possibly pie charts, but I could not confirm which graph types are included.

Chapter 7 Information Processing has several short puzzle-style sections (SET game, map colouring, packing, shopping comparison). These are mapped as partial fits to general reasoning competencies rather than each getting its own competency. Only cryptology received a proposed competency.

sections.title: Rational numbers on a number line
Decimal representation of a rational number
Rational numbers between any two given rational numbers
Basic Arithmetic Operations on Rational Numbers
Word Problems on the basic operations

outcomes.statement: Represent rational numbers on a number line and in standard form, compare them, and find rational numbers between any two given ones.
Add, subtract, multiply and divide rational numbers and solve word problems with them.
Check which properties (closure, commutative, associative, distributive, identity, inverse) hold for rational-number operations.

proposed.name: Use closure, commutative, associative, distributive and identity properties of operations on a number system
proposed.why: Existing list has only MLY.alg.distributive (one property, algebraic); TN teaches the property set explicitly for whole numbers (G6), integers (G7) and rationals (G8).

outcomes.statement: Identify perfect squares and find square roots by prime factorisation and long division, including for decimals, and estimate non-perfect square roots.
Find cubes and cube roots using prime factorisation, and identify perfect cubes.
Simplify expressions with zero and negative integer exponents using the laws of exponents, and write numbers in standard (scientific) form.
Calculate the arc length, area and perimeter of a sector from the radius and the central angle.
Find the perimeter and area of combined shapes made of rectangles, triangles, trapeziums, semicircles and sectors.
Match 3-D solids to their nets and views, and count their faces, edges and vertices to verify Euler's formula.

proposed.name: Count faces, vertices and edges of polyhedra and verify Euler's formula
proposed.why: nets and solid-views do not cover F + V - E = 2 relationships.

sections.title: Word problems that involve linear equations
Graph: To obtain a straight line
Graph: Line parallel to the coordinate axes

outcomes.statement: Multiply polynomials and divide a polynomial by a monomial or binomial.

Factorise expressions by common factors, grouping and standard (including cubic) identities.
Solve linear equations in one variable, including ones with rational coefficients and the variable on both sides, and apply them to word problems.
Plot points in all four quadrants and choose a suitable scale for the axes.
Draw the straight-line graph of a linear relation, including lines parallel to the axes, and read values from it.

outcomes.statement: Solve percentage word problems, including percentage increase and decrease.
Calculate profit, loss, discount, overhead expenses and GST to find marked price, selling price or cost price.
Calculate compound interest with annual, half-yearly or quarterly compounding, apply the formula to growth and depreciation, and compare it with simple interest.

Solve time and work problems using each worker's rate of work per unit time.

Recognise similar triangles (AA, SAS, SSS) and use proportional sides to find unknown lengths.

outcomes.statement: Construct medians, altitudes, perpendicular bisectors and angle bisectors of a triangle and locate the centroid, orthocentre, circumcentre and incentre.

proposed.why: Constructions-bisectors covers bisecting a segment/angle; concurrency points (centroid, orthocentre, circumcentre, incentre) are not covered.

outcomes.statement: Construct a general quadrilateral, a trapezium and special quadrilaterals (parallelogram, rhombus, rectangle, square) from given measurements, and find the area.
